bluf: Bluerank is a Poland based enterprise performance agency founded in 2005 leading with SEO and paid search under official Google and Meta partner status. Its record is quiet: the last dated moves are European Search Awards and Performance Marketing Diamonds wins from 2019 to 2021, with no AI posture line, no pricing and nothing after 2021, so where it is going the record does not say. What a rival should know: it sells paid social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site, 9 of its 10 named clients are names only, and Orange, its most decorated account, also sits on the artefact and semetis books.
doing:
The positioning line reads: customer journey driven agency offering SEO, performance, analytics, media buying, content, social, strategy and creation, backed by in house marketing technologies. In plain words, a full service search and performance shop for large brands that says it builds its own tools, though the record names none. The headline claim is 20+ years supporting the biggest brands online plus official Google and Meta partner status; the 2005 founding year supports the first part.

Service lines run from Digital Strategy and Creation through Social Media, Media Buying, SEO, Content Marketing and Content Ekspert to Performance Marketing, Performance Video, Google Marketing Platform and Marketing Analytics. It leads with Paid Search and SEO, both scored 3: its JSON-LD pairs SEO with PPC and calls it an SEM agency, and a Google Ads case for a premium fashion brand reports ROAS 1500% and doubled conversion value. Core lines scored 2 are Content & Digital PR (European Search Awards 2021 Best Use of Content Marketing with Orange), Data & Measurement (an analytics reporting case for Mennica Polska), Paid Social (a Meta Ads case reporting +480% purchases and ROAS +87% in three months for a fashion brand) and Programmatic & CTV (its one LinkedIn ad pitches Connected TV with Retail Media). Creator, email and retail media score 1; AI search, AI automation, B2B, CRO, local and web build score 0.

On AI the record is silent: no posture line, no capability above 0; the one AI signal is the Sony Centre marketing automation case.

The dated moves are all awards and stop in 2021: 2019 European Search Awards for Mascus and Mall.pl; 2020 for PizzaPortal.pl and Raja; 2021 for Promedica24 and Orange, plus Performance Marketing Diamonds CEE 2021 for Orange and Mitsubishi. No pricing signal is listed. Absent: any move after 2021, news, jobs, offices, an employee count, an owner, a named proprietary tool and a readable sitemap (0 URLs counted).
clients:
The client type is enterprise, the biggest brands online in its own words. The record lists verticals of fashion ecommerce, health, retail and B2B; the home market is Poland, with no offices listed.

The needs read holds 10 clients, one observed and 9 named only. The observed one is Sony Centre, whose case slug reads marketing automation that sells annual revenue in a month, coded CRM and owned audiences plus AI and automation. Two more are case studies with no work read: Mennica Polska, though the Data & Measurement note credits the case with streamlining its analytics reporting, and Rainbow, an 18 year client relationship per the prominence note. The remaining seven are award entries on the about page, Orange, Mitsubishi, Promedica24, PizzaPortal.pl, Raja, Mascus and Mall.pl, which the table marks named only; the award notes still give the shape of the work: local PPC for PizzaPortal.pl and Promedica24, B2B PPC for Raja, retail search for Mall.pl, a pan European campaign for Mascus, content marketing and a sales campaign for Orange and crisis creativity for Mitsubishi, which against the taxonomy read as paid performance, organic demand and content signals inferred from award categories.

One client is shared: Orange also appears on the artefact and semetis books, so it shops across tracked agencies. The evidence types are case study (3) and award entry (7).

What the base needs next: the mix is most exposed to KJ6, the agency middle is being hollowed out, on paid search, SEO and paid social hours. It is likely, moderate confidence, that fashion ecommerce and retail accounts next ask for feed, entity and answer visibility work (P1 and P2 are absent here) and for owned audience automation of the Sony Centre kind, and unlikely that they keep buying PPC hours at the same price under KJ6.
house:
Say and do: two lines tested with a result, one practised, integrity 50. Paid Social is contradicted: it sells paid social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site. LinkedIn advertising is corroborated: 1 company page ad of its own, pitching Connected TV with Retail Media as 2026 ad cost optimization. Paid Search is unknown because the Transparency Center lookup was blocked, and publishing cadence is unknown, not measured: the record counts 0 sitemap URLs, 0 updated in 90 or 365 days and 0 AI topic URLs, so content velocity cannot be read.

The flagged gap is the missing social pixel. There is no llms.txt and no AI crawler is blocked. The stack is GTM, VWO and Cookiebot on WordPress, with VWO the one test tool detected; no social pixels and no ABM stack. Google ads: blocked lookup, no count. Meta and TikTok: the record is silent. Social links point to LinkedIn and Instagram.
market:
Horus reads a tailwind index of minus 3.9, band Neutral. Best placed for KJ8, human provenance becomes a distribution signal (net 0.159, Creator & Influencer and Content & Digital PR), and KJ2, ads inside AI answers (net 0.154, Paid Search). Most exposed to KJ6, the agency middle is being hollowed out (net minus 0.318, Paid Search, SEO and Paid Social), and KJ5, the price of attention splits in two (net minus 0.159). The mix sits at 17:41 on the Solar Arc; best fit is The Walled Oasis at 47/100. It is making P4 (supply the inputs automation runs on), partial on P7, absent on P1, P2, P6 and P8, unknown on P5; P3 does not apply.

The Monsoon read is 40.4, Breeze: migration 35.4 against displacement 45.4, SEO (16) and Paid Search (11) carrying the most movable hours, automation overlapping 30% of them. Shore: 75% South and Southeast Asia, 15% Eastern Europe. Two inferred terms, destination and icp_enterprise, pull the index down; no hub office is listed; the onshore claim in its own words is in house marketing technologies.
openings:
The strongest opening is the paid social contradiction: Bluerank is a Meta partner selling paid social on a +480% purchases case, and its own site runs no social ad pixel. A rival showing its own pixel and Meta ads is likely, moderate confidence, to turn that into a credibility question in any fashion ecommerce pitch. Falsifier: a social pixel appearing on bluerank.com at the next compile.

Second, the AI gap is total: no AI search, no automation capability, no llms.txt, P1 and P2 absent, so an audited answer visibility offer to its retail and fashion accounts is very likely, high confidence, something it cannot match from the record. Third, Orange shops: it appears on the artefact and semetis books too, so the most decorated account is contestable, roughly even chance. Fourth, 9 of 10 clients show no described work, a question to ask each. Fifth, no public pricing (P5 unknown) leaves room for an outcome priced offer. Price is a weak lever: Monsoon reads Breeze at 40.4 and the destination term marks Poland as a delivery geography itself, so an offshore undercut is unlikely to bite; the pitch is capability and freshness, since no move is dated after 2021.
watch: Indicator I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, reads October 2026: output or outcome pricing at a top five holdco would deepen KJ6, the judgment this mix is most exposed to.
Indicator I4, Meta Q3 2026 average price per ad, reads late October 2026: at or above +5% continues walled garden inflation under KJ5, pressing the paid social and CTV lines.

Indicator I6, platform AI labeling enforcement after the EU Article 50(2) deadline, reads 2 December 2026: new reach penalties for unlabeled AI personas would strengthen KJ8, its best placed judgment, through the content line.
Follow up whether any move dated after 2021 appears, whether a proprietary tool is named behind the in house marketing technologies claim, and whether Orange stays on the artefact and semetis books.
